Negative: order creation without the Idempotency-Key header must be rejected with 400. Idempotency keys are mandatory so network retries can never create duplicate orders.
Negative: an empty Idempotency-Key header is equivalent to missing and must be rejected with 400.
Negative: batch order creation also requires the Idempotency-Key header; missing it must return 400.
Negative: an unsupported payment method must fail with 400 before any money moves (server-side normalization rejects unknown enums).
Boundary: a non-numeric order id in the path is a type mismatch and must be rejected with 400, not 500.
Boundary: a negative order id never exists and must yield 404, never 500.
Boundary: an order id far above any real row must return 404.
Boundary: page size above the 100 cap is clamped, so a huge size still returns 200 with a bounded payload.
Boundary: size=0 is clamped to the minimum of 1, so the call still succeeds with 200.
Negative: quantity must be positive (@Positive); -1 must be rejected with 400.
Negative: quantity is required (@NotNull); omitting it must be rejected with 400.
Negative: reordering an order id that does not exist must return 404.

Security: a classic SQL injection fragment in the keyword must be treated as plain text (parameterized queries) and return 200 — never 500 or a data leak. A 400 from the WAF security policy is also an acceptable safe outcome.
Security: a path-traversal fragment in the keyword must be treated as plain text and return 200.
Security: control characters in the email must be rejected cleanly (400) — never 500 or authentication bypass.
